newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices fall on stockpiling.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices fall on stockpiling.

text.p: Indian sugar prices fell on Wednesday as millers unloaded stocks triggering more supplies in the market, dealers said.
"Consumer demand and enquiries from the retailers remained sluggish while fresh arrivals sparked fresh offerings," one dealer said.

Free sale quota for the current month is lower but negligible demand prompted millers to unload stock which in turn triggered more supplies in the market. Free sale quota for current month is 650,000 tonnes, while it was 800,000 tonnes last month.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 slid by 5/10 rupees to 1,240/1,270 rupees per quintal while M-30 fell by 5 rupees per quintal to 1,280/1,370 rupees per quintal.
Sugar mill delivery moved down to 1,170/1,195 rupees from 1,185/1,205 rupees per quintal.

Bombay sugar market will remain officially closed on Thursday for birth centenary of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose, noted freedom fighter. Market will reopen for trading on Friday, dealer said. -Bombay Commodities +91-22-265 9000
